title: T1055.011 — Process Injection - Extra Window Memory Injection
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Process Injection - Extra Window Memory Injection with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated simulation of Extra Window Memory Injection in eight steps. A phishing loader enumerates a window with spare class memory, writes shellcode into it with SetWindowLongPtr, swaps the window procedure with GWLP_WNDPROC, triggers it with SendMessage, stages a memory-only implant, beacons to a C2 server, and defenders isolate the host and capture memory. Hover any node for details.

steps.title: Foothold
steps.caption: A small loader process starts with normal user rights inside the user session
steps.defender: EDR shows a suspicious new process under the user session, started from the Downloads folder.

steps.title: Window hunt
steps.caption: It looks for a window whose class reserves enough spare bytes: cbWndExtra of 8 bytes or more on 64-bit Windows
steps.defender: window enumeration is quiet. Native logs show almost nothing, so this stage often has no direct evidence.

steps.title: Chunked writes
steps.caption: The loader writes position-independent shellcode into the spare bytes, chunk by chunk, using SetWindowLongPtr with a new offset for every write.
steps.defender: an EDR user-mode hook, or Sysmon Event 10 (ProcessAccess), can record the cross-process writes against the GUI process.

steps.title: Memory-only staging
steps.caption: It never writes a new file to disk, so file-based antivirus has nothing to scan
steps.defender: a memory scan finds an unbacked read-write-execute (RWX) region inside the signed GUI process.
